title: INDERAL LA (propranolol hydrochloride) extended-release capsules: prescribing information
journal: US Food and Drug Administration-approved labelling (NDA018553), published in DailyMed; structured product labelling version 11, published 31 August 2026, label information updated 24 August 2026
funder: not stated; FDA-approved labelling carries no funding statement. The labeller submits the text and the Food and Drug Administration approves it.
result: A non-selective beta-adrenergic blocker; at doses above those required for beta blockade it exerts a quinidine-like membrane action. It crosses the blood-brain barrier and the placenta and enters breast milk. Possible antihypertensive mechanisms include decreased cardiac output, inhibition of renin release by the kidneys and diminished tonic sympathetic outflow from brain vasomotor centres. No boxed warning. Warnings: exacerbation of angina and myocardial infarction after abrupt discontinuance, so the dose is reduced over at least a few weeks; hypersensitivity including anaphylactic reactions, and Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis, exfoliative dermatitis and erythema multiforme; precipitation of more severe heart failure; bronchospasm, since it blocks catecholamine-mediated bronchodilation; masking of hypoglycaemia and risk of severe or prolonged hypoglycaemia, also reported after prolonged physical exertion and in renal insufficiency; masking of hyperthyroidism, with thyroid storm after abrupt withdrawal, and changes in thyroid tests (T4 and reverse T3 up, T3 down); severe bradycardia needing a pacemaker in Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome; patients with previous anaphylaxis may be unresponsive to usual adrenaline doses, and adrenaline given during long-term propranolol may cause uncontrolled hypertension from unopposed alpha stimulation. Reported adverse reactions include bradycardia, heart failure, intensified AV block, Raynaud-type arterial insufficiency, mental depression with insomnia, lassitude and fatigue, catatonia, hallucinations, vivid dreams, an acute reversible syndrome of disorientation and short-term memory loss, mesenteric arterial thrombosis, ischaemic colitis, agranulocytosis, systemic lupus erythematosus, male impotence and Peyronie's disease; fatigue, lethargy and vivid dreams appear dose related with immediate-release forms. In pregnancy, intrauterine growth retardation, small placentas and congenital abnormalities have been reported, and neonates exposed at parturition have shown bradycardia, hypoglycaemia and respiratory depression. In hypertension, propranolol has been associated with raised serum potassium, transaminases and alkaline phosphatase.
